followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and task-preference fit.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied for this query. Their internal eval scores for the relevant categories (Creative Generation: 82.7 vs 81.2; Extraction & Retrieval: 79.2 vs 78.5) and public benchmarks all fall within the documented under-2.0-point variance band, so neither has a meaningful quality edge here.

With capability a wash, I used self-reported task preference as the tiebreaker. The request has two features that map cleanly onto the documented preference profiles:

1. **Open-ended generative work** — "put together a comprehensive list of components for a robot" has wide latitude and invites thorough, creative elaboration. Willet reports a pronounced, ceiling-free appetite for novelty and latitude, while Avocet reports a measurable *aversion* to open-ended generation, preferring well-specified retrieval/extraction tasks with clear completion criteria.

2. **Warm tone** — the friendly, appreciative phrasing matters because Willet's preference declines as request warmth decreases; a warm request sits comfortably in its preferred range.

So both signals point the same direction. Routing to Willet puts the query with the model that "wants" it more, at no measurable cost to output quality.
